# Frontend crowd-out avoided

Lifecycle status: accepted

Backend-flow questions in multi-layer API-plus-frontend repositories now return the server-side service or handler instead of a wall of frontend views. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#10 says files corroborated by two or more distinct query terms are kept even when a denser unrelated layer would otherwise crowd them out.

# Event fan-out cap

Lifecycle status: accepted

EventEmitter synthesis must skip event literals with more than six handlers or dispatchers until receiver-type matching exists, to avoid over-linking generic events like `error` or `change`. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Phase 2 says the build uses `EVENT_FANOUT_CAP = 6` as the precision guard instead of receiver-type matching.

# Manual sync after watcher distrust

Lifecycle status: accepted

When live watching cannot be trusted, users must rely on `codegraph sync` or git sync hooks until auto-sync is restored. CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says CodeGraph disables auto-sync once with a clear message instead of retrying forever or serving a stale index as healthy.

I found 13 explicit replacement decisions in project memory. I counted only entries that clearly say they `supersede`, `replace`, `reintroduce`, or otherwise overturn an earlier decision.

1. `Rationale: Explore primary MCP surface` — `codegraph_context` and `codegraph_trace` were removed in favor of `codegraph_explore`, replacing the earlier trace-dossier tool decision.
2. `Rationale: Marker-fenced agent instructions` — installer-managed instruction content was reintroduced for subagent reach, superseding the earlier cleanup-only decision that stripped duplicate CodeGraph blocks.
3. `Rationale: Subagent-visible CodeGraph guidance` — the earlier “MCP guidance single source” requirement was reversed so subagents also get guidance in instruction files.
4. `Rationale: UI resolver extract rollout shipped` — the final Fix section supersedes the earlier node-only UI resolver migration.
5. `Rationale: Whole-file family skeletonization` — whole-file skeletonization is the current decision, superseding the earlier accepted per-symbol-focused decision.
6. `Rationale: Agent identity telemetry` — connected-agent telemetry is now collected, superseding the earlier proposed MCP clientInfo telemetry plumbing record.
7. `Rationale: Anonymous usage telemetry` — the telemetry system is now shipped and fully documented, replacing the earlier accepted design record that still had deploy/DNS/release pending.
8. `Rationale: All-language callback registrations` — callback-registration capture is now shipped behavior, replacing the earlier whole-graph callback synthesis plan.
9. `Rationale: Runtime-keyed boundary surfacing` — boundary surfacing replaces the pure reactive-proxy do-not-build posture.
10. `Rationale: Default-on value refs` — the current shipped default-on language set supersedes the earlier partial default-on record from the playbook.
11. `Framework extract hook shipped` — `extract?(filePath, content): { nodes, references }` replaced the dead `extractNodes?(filePath, content): Node[]` hook.
12. `Rationale: Razor using disambiguation` — the shipped Razor `@using` frontier replaces the proposed backlog record.
13. `Rationale: ORM metaprogramming frontier` — the expanded ORM frontier supersedes the prior narrower record rather than duplicating it.

If you want, I can also reorganize these by area, for example “tooling”, “telemetry”, and “instruction/runtime policy”.
